Ari (Finance): Hey team — noticed a small but consistent dip in billed embed counts for AcmeCorp after last night's index migration. Invoice for March shows ~12k fewer embeds than our ingestion logs. Anyone seen this?
Maeve (Eng): Looking now. Which pipeline and index? Did we change any TTL / dedupe logic during migration?
Ari (Finance): migration ran for embed-index-v2 -> v3 at 03:12 UTC. No intentional dedupe changes but v3 changed the primary key form (doc_id + shard -> doc_hash) and we added a short-lived index cache. Billing shows 12,347 fewer embed events between 03:10 and 04:30 UTC.
Maeve (Eng): OK I ran a quick query against the event stream. Short excerpt:
```
SELECT count(*) FROM embed_events
WHERE customer_id = 'acme' AND received_at BETWEEN '2025-03-14T03:00:00Z' AND '2025-03-14T05:00:00Z';
-- result: 87,653
```
and the billing-metered table shows 75,306 for same window. So ~12,347 delta matches.
Ravi (Billing): Do we know if the missing rows were dropped (never ingested) or just not joined into the meter pipeline?
Maeve (Eng): From logs, the index migration introduced a new step that emits a dedupe token to the metering router. There's a bug where the token expires (ttl=30s) before the router acknowledges under heavy traffic bursts. If TTL expired, router treats event as duplicate and discards.
Tom (SRE): I see transient backpressure on the router at 03:20-03:35 UTC, CPU spikes on router-2 and a few 429s from the rate limiter. Those lines align with the delta.
Ari (Finance): So this is a metering-loss due to TTL/dedup race, not a billing miscount in aggregation? Will it affect historically closed invoices or just current cycle?
Maeve (Eng): It's a loss at ingestion time — events never made it into the metering ledger. That means invoices for March were calculated from the ledger missing those rows. We can either: 1) surface an invoice adjustment for Acme, or 2) reconstruct events and run a targeted backfill into the ledger.
Ravi (Billing): What's the risk/cost for a backfill? Need estimate before we reach out to Acme support. Also, are other customers affected?
Maeve (Eng): Preliminary scan: ~0.1% of total embed events across customers in that window. Most impact concentrated on Acme and two other high-throughput tenants. Backfill plan: rehydrate events from raw ingestion stream, dedupe using stable doc_hash and force-write to ledger with a backfill_tag. I estimated 15k rows for Acme, 7k + 4k for the others. No model calls or embed regen required — purely ledger writes.
Ravi (Billing): Cost estimate for ledger write + reconciliation job? (ballpark)
Maeve (Eng): Compute/time: a cron backfill job ~2 vCPU, 4GB, runs for ~45m. Storage/DB ops trivial. Engineering hours for coord: ~2-3h. No additional per-token charges because we're not re-running model inference.
Tom (SRE): We'll need a maintenance window to avoid clobbering current writes. Suggest 03:00–04:30 UTC next Saturday for the backfill. We'll throttle to <5% of normal ingestion.
Ari (Finance): OK sounds reasonable. If we backfill, we should prepare an invoice note and an adjustment line item for Acme; prefer to be transparent. Ravi — approve backfill? Cap on hours/cost?
Ravi (Billing): Approve conditional on: engineering confirms no chance of double-billing and we add a backfill_flag on rows + metadata; cap infra spend to <$200 for the job. Also we should include a one-line credit if Acme prefers a manual adjustment instead of a corrected invoice.
Maeve (Eng): Will add backfill_flag + backfill_run_id to every inserted row and a reconciliation report. No double-billing: billing only reads ledger rows with finality=true and source!='estimated'; we'll mark backfill rows source='backfill' and finality=true.
Ari (Finance): Great. @Tom please schedule the job for Sat 03:00 UTC and post the run id. I'll prep the customer-facing note once we have reconciliation numbers. :+1:
Tom (SRE): Scheduled -> backfill-run-20250321-01. I'll post a short run playbook in #release-war-room and notify oncall.
billing-bot: Invoice generation for AcmeCorp (2025-03) completed at 05:12 UTC — amount $12,345.67. Note: pending adjustments subject to reconciliation.
Maeve (Eng): I'll kick off the rehydration dry-run tonight on a staging subset and post counts. If dry-run matches the delta we can proceed with production.
Ravi (Billing): Thanks. Please include the reconciliation CSV (ledger vs raw) and a summary line: rows_added, customer_id, tokens_added, run_id.
Ari (Finance): Thanks everyone — please keep updates in this thread.
Maeve (Eng): Will do — posting dry-run results in ~2h.
